header.title: The Battle of France
header.hook: Six weeks. One of Europe's great armies, defeated.
header.outro: France would stay divided until the liberation of 1944.
header.footnote: Fronts simplified; losses interpolated between sourced totals.

territories.note: Wikipedia: German invasion of the Netherlands; German invasion of Belgium (1940); Frieser ch.4 | conf: medium (NL/Albert Canal); low in Ardennes (fluid, end-of-day guess ±20 km). The Hague airborne landings omitted (mostly defeated 10 May).

Wikipedia: German invasion of the Netherlands (9th Pz at Moerdijk 16:45 12 May); Battle of Hannut; Frieser | conf: medium. Grebbe line intact; Dordrecht contested; Liège forts still Belgian (ignored).

Wikipedia: Battle of Sedan (1940); German bombing of Rotterdam; Frieser ch.5-6 | conf: medium. Sedan bridgehead ~20x15 km (1st Pz over Ardennes canal at Omicourt); Dinant/Monthermé bridgeheads small. Fortress Holland still Dutch until evening capitulation.

Wikipedia: German invasion of the Netherlands (capitulation signed Rijsoord 15 May); Battle of France (Monthermé, Montcornet); Frieser | conf: medium; Montcornet tip (6th Pz) is a thin column, not a held front. Zeeland still Allied.

Wikipedia: German invasion of Belgium (Brussels occupied 17 May; withdrawal Senne/Dendre/Scheldt 16-19 May); Battle of Montcornet; Frieser | conf: medium-low. Maubeuge fortress and Mormal forest Allied remnants simplified; Guderian tip at Oise (Moy/Ribemont).

Wikipedia: German invasion of Belgium (Scheldt line night 18/19; Antwerp fell 18/19 May); Battle of France (Péronne, Somme bridgehead) | conf: medium-low. Added keyframe: Escaut line + Péronne. Laon still French (de Gaulle attacked from Laon 19 May).

Wikipedia: Battle of France (2nd Pz recon at Noyelles-sur-Mer 20 May; Amiens and Abbeville taken); Frieser ch.7 | conf: medium. Corridor north edge (Arras-Doullens-Hesdin-Authie) ±10 km; Arras still British.

Wikipedia: Dunkirk evacuation (halt order 23/24 May); Siege of Calais; Battle of Boulogne; Battle of the Lys (1940) | conf: medium. Aa canal bridgeheads (St-Omer, St-Pierre-Brouck) small; Belgian line Lys-Schipdonk-Leopold canal.

Wikipedia: Siege of Calais (fell 26 May); Battle of the Lys; Dunkirk evacuation (halt rescinded 26 May) | conf: low-medium. Added keyframe (pocket changes fast 24->28). Belgian line after Kortrijk breach approximated.

Wikipedia: German invasion of Belgium (surrender 04:00 28 May); Battle of Dunkirk (perimeter Nieuwpoort-Veurne-Bergues-Gravelines); Siege of Lille | conf: medium-low. BEF corridor Ypres-Poperinge-Cassel collapsing; Lille pocket ~35-40k French (to 31 May).

Wikipedia: Dunkirk evacuation (daily lifts; Lille surrendered 31 May); Battle of Dunkirk | conf: medium. Perimeter on the French side of the border after British left De Panne/Nieuwpoort 31 May-1 June. Abbeville bridgehead partly reduced (not shown).
Wikipedia: Dunkirk evacuation (last lift night 3/4 June; ~35-40k French rearguard captured 4 June) | conf: low-medium. Optional keyframe: final inner perimeter (Malo-Rosendael-Teteghem-Coudekerque).
Wikipedia: Fall Rot (offensive opens 5 June on the Somme) | conf: same as 4 June (start line).

Rommel/7th Pz: Hangest breakthrough 5-7 June, Forges-les-Eaux 7 June, Rouen 9 June (Wikipedia Fall Rot; Battle of France) | conf: low-medium. Added keyframe for the non-linear Rommel thrust; Hoepner/Kleist gains at Amiens/Péronne only 15-30 km.

FR Wikipedia Bataille de France (Seine reached at Rouen 9 June); Wikipedia Fall Rot (Army Group A attacks on Aisne 9 June) | conf: low-medium. IX Corps/51st Div cut off west of Rouen (Pays de Caux) - Allied by being west of the line.

Wikipedia: Operation Cycle (Le Havre held to 13 June; 51st Div surrender 12 June); Fall Rot (Marne crossed at Château-Thierry, Guderian at Châlons) | conf: low-medium. Le Havre pocket = area west of first points.

Wikipedia: Fall Rot (Paris occupied 14 June); Battle of Saumur (government left Tours 14 June) | conf: low-medium. Seine estuary to Troyes and Saint-Dizier; Operation Tiger (Saar) opens 14 June, not shown.

Wikipedia: Battle of France (XIX Korps at Swiss border 17 June; Pétain asks for armistice 17 June); FR Wikipedia (Orléans/Loire 16 June, Pontarlier 17, Belfort 18) | conf: low. Rommel's Cotentin thrust and Lorraine pocket edges ±20-30 km; pocket = French 2nd Army Group (3rd/5th/8th Armies) + Maginot.

Wikipedia: Battle of Saumur (Loire 19-21 June); Fall Rot (Cherbourg 18/19, Brest 19/20); FR Wikipedia (Lyon 19-20 June) | conf: low. South-of-Loire wedge to the Cher/Châteauroux/Vichy approximate; Lorient (fell 21) treated as German.

Wikipedia: Second Armistice at Compiègne (signed 22 June 18:50); Montluçon/Clermont occupied 21 June (Touret); Romans 22 June (local chronology) | conf: low. Vosges pocket (Condé) surrendered 22 June. South-central tip positions vary by source.

FR Wikipedia Bataille de France (ceasefire 25 June 00:35; Clermont, Angoulême reached); Italian occupation of France (832 km2); labatailledesalpes.fr (Voreppe 23-24 June) | conf: low for the ceasefire line (no atlas map found; ±25 km in Charente/Limousin/Loire). Bordeaux NOT reached by 25 June per most accounts (entered ~30 June; FR Wikipedia claims 24 June).

events.title: Invasion
events.text: Germany invades the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg.

events.title: Eben-Emael
events.text: Glider troops take Belgium's strongest fort.

events.title: Sedan
events.text: German armour crosses the Meuse at Sedan and Dinant.

events.title: Rotterdam
events.text: The Luftwaffe bombs Rotterdam; 711 killed.

events.title: The Netherlands
events.text: The Dutch army capitulates.

events.title: Brussels
events.text: German troops enter Brussels.

events.title: The Channel
events.text: Panzers reach the sea at Abbeville. The Allies are cut in two.

events.title: Arras
events.text: A British-French counterattack briefly checks Rommel.

events.title: Halt order
events.text: Hitler stops the panzers on the Aa canal.

events.title: Dunkirk
events.text: Calais falls. The evacuation begins.

events.title: Belgium
events.text: The Belgian army capitulates.

events.title: Dunkirk ends
events.text: 338,226 Allied soldiers reach Britain.

events.title: Fall Rot
events.text: Germany attacks across the Somme.

events.title: Italy
events.text: Italy declares war. The French government leaves Paris.

events.title: Saint-Valery
events.text: The British 51st Highland Division surrenders.

events.title: Paris
events.text: German troops enter Paris unopposed.

events.title: Cut off
events.text: Guderian reaches the Swiss border. Pétain asks for terms.

events.title: De Gaulle
events.text: From London, de Gaulle calls on France to fight on.

events.title: Cherbourg
events.text: Rommel takes Cherbourg.

events.title: Armistice
events.text: Signed at Compiègne, in the same railway carriage as 1918.

events.title: Ceasefire
events.text: The fighting stops at 00:35.

events.title: France divided
events.text: Germany occupies the north and the Atlantic coast.

youtube.title: The Battle of France, Day by Day (1940)
youtube.summary: The fall of France in 1940, day by day on one map: the invasion of the Low Countries, the breakthrough at Sedan, Dunkirk, the fall of Paris and the armistice.
